name: issue_1066_cold_morning_mild_day_arms_heat_immediately
description: Cold morning on a mild day, thermostat still left in cool from yesterday afternoon. Indoor is 66F, 2F below comfort_heat (68F). Nearest-edge arming (Issue #1066, docs/08 section 6f) must switch the thermostat to heat on the FIRST evaluation, with no recency window, deadband, sustain wait or dwell lock. Before #1066 a mild day defaulted to the ceiling edge and the house sat below the floor in cool mode for roughly 11 minutes (live incident 2026-10-11).
source: Issue #1066 live incident 2026-10-11 (seventh recurrence of the mild/warm-day wrong-edge class: #821, #823, #827, #843, #858, #867, #1048 comment)
notes: Occupant impact: the person wakes up in a 66F house and the thermostat is in cool mode. They must get heat immediately, not after a breach/deadband/sustain/lock sequence.

(a) Scenario effectiveness: if nearest-edge arming were deleted, the mild-day classification would arm the day-type default edge (ceiling, cool). On origin/main comfort_family_decision.py, a mild day is natively 'cooling' and heat is the against-grain direction, which needs a floor breach beyond the mild deadband (and, under #843, a recency check) PLUS a 90 s sustain confirmation before escalating; on the first evaluation the FSM only arms a candidate and stays cooling. The comfort_family_switch_by(heating, 06:00:00), comfort_family=heating and last_hvac_mode=heat assertions would therefore all fail on the old behavior, because nothing is evaluated a second time in this event list.

(b) Docs vs production: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md section 6f, rule row 'indoor < floor -> heating, breach: immediate' and the 'Before / after' row 'Mild/warm day, indoor falls below the floor'.

(c) Occupant outcome if this test fails to catch a regression: the household wakes to a cold house with the furnace idle and the AC armed until a multi-minute confirmation sequence completes, repeating the incident that was reported seven times.
Classification fields: day_type=mild with hvac_mode=off and windows_recommended=true match what classifier.py derives for DAY_TYPE_MILD (not hand-overridden).

events.note: Wake-up: indoor 66F, 2F below comfort_heat(68). Thermostat is still in cool from the previous afternoon.
Mild-day classification, first evaluation of the morning. indoor(66) < floor(68) is a breach: heat must be armed now, regardless of the day-type default (ceiling).

assertions.reason: Floor breach arms heat on the very first evaluation (no sustain wait, no recency window): the comfort_family_switch event carries resolved_family=heating at the classification timestamp.
The switch is flagged as a breach (indoor already below the floor), which is what lets it bypass the 600 s anti-chatter dwell lock.
Engine state confirms the heating family is armed, not merely an emitted event.
The commanded thermostat mode is heat (a real climate service call at comfort_heat), replacing the leftover cool mode.

verdict.summary: A cold morning on a mild day arms heat on the first evaluation instead of waiting out breach, deadband, sustain and dwell gates.
verdict.observed_behavior: Indoor 66F below the 68F floor with the thermostat in cool: the selector emits comfort_family_switch(heating, breach=true) at the first classification and commands heat.
verdict.expected_behavior: Below the floor always means heat, immediately, on every day type (docs/08 section 6f).
